primary_source.paper: Wu, H., Han, Z., Zhou, J.T., Huang, H., Zhang, C., "Computational Reasoning of Large Language Models" (Turing Machine Bench / TMBench)

trace_source: vendor/TMBench-repo/src/prompt.py, generate_prompt(): the worked '## Example:' block baked into the official evaluation prompt template (m=2, alphabet {A,B,C}, init [B C A]); saved verbatim to published_trace.txt
format_description: Each step is a '### step N:' block giving the Head Symbol read from the front of a symbol queue, a one-line prose Action describing the append/delete performed under the m-tag rewrite rule, and the resulting Queue State as a bracketed, space-separated symbol list, ending in '<halt>' once the queue is shorter than the fixed deletion count m.
theory_citation: Ladner, R.E. (1975), 'The Circuit Value Problem is Log Space Complete for P', ACM SIGACT News 7(1), DOI 10.1145/990518.990519 -- the standard theoretical grounding for 'simulate this deterministic machine for T steps and report the result' being P-complete (a bounded-time TM run compiles into a size-O(T) circuit, and evaluating it is CVP-hard), i.e. inherently serial unless P=NC; see also Greenlaw, Hoover & Ruzzo (1995), 'Limits to Parallel Computation: P-Completeness Theory', for the general theory. This is the benchmark's 'maximally serial' anchor row: a random small transition table has no exploitable algebraic structure (unlike Rule 90's GF(2) linearity in the cellular_automaton task), so no known shortcut exists. Separately, TMBench's own m-tag-system formalism (the vendored primary_source) is a different but comparably hard serial rewriting system -- tag systems are known Turing-universal (Cocke, J. & Minsky, M. (1964), 'Universality of tag systems with P=2', J. ACM 11(1)) -- which is why it was usable as a stand-in published trace, but it is not itself the cited authority for our task's P-completeness claim.

knob.name: depth
knob.granularity: integer m-tag rewrite-step count; defaults match TMBench src/tag_generate.py -- delete_count m=2, alphabet_size=5 ({A,B,C,D,E}), rule production length 1-5, initial queue length 2-9

published_data.paper: Wu, Han, Zhou, Huang, Zhang (2025), 'Computational Reasoning of Large Language Models' (TMBench), arXiv:2504.20771
published_data.metric: step-wise LLM simulation accuracy of an m-tag rewriting system as a function of step count (controllable difficulty), correlated against established reasoning benchmarks (AIME 2024, MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro) as a cross-domain computational-reasoning proxy
published_data.models: Gemini, Gemma, DeepSeek, Qwen, LLaMA, Grok, Claude, GPT, and Doubao families per the repo's acknowledgements (e.g. results/TMBench_gemini-2.5-pro-exp-03-25_chat.json is one full per-sample transcript vendored in vendor/TMBench-repo); exact model/version list and numeric accuracy table not extracted from the PDF in this desk pass
published_data.values: not extracted numerically here; abstract reports 'clear step-wise accuracy curves' and 'strong correlations with real-world tasks' but gives no numbers outside figures/tables in the PDF body

notes: No paper or benchmark was found that publishes an LLM-facing trace of the literal task assigned here -- a random small Turing machine with an explicit (head state, head position, tape) triple shown per step (see SOURCING.md: GitHub/HF/arXiv/CLRS/lm-evaluation-harness/BIG-bench search all came up empty for that exact formalism). TMBench (vendored in vendor/TMBench-repo, cloned from the paper's own GitHub, superseding the HF-dataset-only mirror originally vendored in vendor/Turing-Machine-Bench/) is the closest published proxy: an m-tag string-rewriting system with a head-symbol read, append/delete rewrite, and per-step queue-state trace -- serial, P-hard-adjacent (tag systems are Turing-universal), and it is the only located source with an actual worked CoT exemplar, so it is used here as primary_source/trace_source for desk-metric purposes even though it is NOT the formalism our task.py will implement. This does not reverse the SOURCING.md 'must write' recommendation: TMBench's fixed sample bank and headless (no separate state/position registers) tag-system format still can't be wrapped as the (head state, head position, tape) simulator this task needs; it only supplies real tokenizer counts and a citable published_data row that the actual task lacked on its own. state_bits/answer_space/knob use this repo's own default knob values (num_states=3, tape_length=6, binary alphabet), NOT TMBench's parameters, since those are definitional properties of the task as assigned rather than of the borrowed trace. tokens_per_step/tokens_total were measured with real tokenizer.json files (tokenizers==0.21.1, already installed): Qwen/Qwen2-7B-Instruct fetched directly from HF; google/gemma-2-2b-it and meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct are gated (401 unauthorized), so unsloth/gemma-2-2b-it and unsloth/llama-3-8b-Instruct / NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct mirrors were used instead (same base tokenizer as the gated originals). state_atomic_tokens=true was verified directly (not assumed): a leading-space single-letter symbol like ' A' encodes to exactly one token in all three tokenizers (e.g. Gemma2 '_A'->id 235... single piece, Llama3/Qwen2 'ĠA' single piece). CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (implementation phase, AMENDMENT 3): task.py implements the m-tag system of primary_source (TMBench), NOT the head-state/position/tape TM sketched in SOURCING.md, so the four fields that were computed from the abandoned 6-cell-binary-tape/3-state formalism have been corrected to describe the implemented task: state_bounded true->false (the queue grows by mean(rule length) - m = +1 symbol per step, so state size scales with depth: |queue| ~= |init| + depth, ~41 symbols at depth 30 with the default knobs); state_bits 10.17->null (no single value exists for an unbounded state; it is depth-dependent, approximately log2(5) * (|init| + depth) ~= 2.32 * (6 + depth) bits); answer_space 64->null (unbounded -- the answer is the final queue, whose length grows with depth); knob.tokens_flat_across_knob true->false (each step line restates the whole queue, so tokens per step grow linearly in depth). Everything else, including all tokenizer measurements, describes the published TMBench trace and is unchanged.
